panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Hand radiograph of the captioned 13-year-old WRS patient; panel-specific caption and in-text evidence attribute cone-shaped/dysplastic phalangeal epiphyses, short tubular bones with tubulation defects and small irregular carpal bones with dysplastic epiphyses to Figure 1A — classic WRS skeletal dysplasia. B: Lateral spine radiograph of the same WRS patient; caption states dorsal vertebral bodies are flattened with anterior edge defects (mild platyspondyly per in-text), a classic WRS skeletal manifestation; platyspondyly has no vocabulary key so it is recorded as a proposed finding. C: Pelvis radiograph of the same 13-year-old WRS patient; caption directly describes hypoplastic acetabular roofs and dysplastic capital femoral epiphyses, classic WRS hip involvement, so disease attribution is unambiguous.

findings.evidence: in-text: 'he had a protuberant abdomen, lumbar lordosis and extension limitation in all joints (Figure 1)'

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph (panel A) of the reported child with Wolcott-Rallison syndrome (article title: WRS due to a novel EIF2AK3 R491X mutation). The in-text explicitly attributes the posture findings to Figure 1: protuberant abdomen, lumbar lordosis and extension limitation in all joints. Lumbar lordosis is a listed WRS finding and is visible in the posture photo; the protuberant abdomen is clearly present and stated in the text but absent from the vocabulary, so it is proposed. Real human-patient image, adequately lit light skin, pediatric growth parameters (height 102.6 cm, growth velocity 2 cm/yr) support child age group, no third-party copyright, and the eye bar is anonymization rather than a clinical annotation.

plate_findings.evidence: Short and broad metacarpi and phalanges
The epiphyses of the humeri are broadened

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Hand radiograph of Patient 1 from a Wolcott-Rallison syndrome (EIF2AK3) case report showing characteristic spondylo-epiphyseal dysplasia features: short and broad metacarpals/phalanges and porotic bones, matching shortened hand bones and generalized osteopenia; the hypoplastic dot-like bony islands are captured as a proposed finding. Pediatric skeleton and in-text developmental delay support child age group. B: Chest-humeri radiograph of the same Patient 1 with Wolcott-Rallison syndrome showing broadened (dysplastic) humeral epiphyses, a recognized spondylo-epiphyseal dysplasia manifestation of WRS; vertebrae are stated to be normal, so no vertebral finding is tagged.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Front-view clinical photograph of Patient 2, a 4.4-year-old child with Wolcott-Rallison syndrome (EIF2AK3 mutation) per the article title and in-text description. The visible short trunk with barrel-shaped chest supports the configured barrel-chest finding; skin tone judged from the well-lit photograph; ethnicity not stated in caption or in-text, so left null. He was born full term by caesarean section with a birth weight of 2.4 Kg (< 5th percentile) which was considered small for gestational age. Neonatal diabetes had been diagnosed at 2 months of age when he presented with poor feeding and dehydration. Treatment with regular and NPH insulin was started for him twice daily upon diagnosis.
